about: Accepted high and critical npm advisories in mobile's shipped dependency tree (npm audit --omit=dev).
Read by infra/scripts/check-npm-audit.py in the mobile CI job. An advisory not listed here fails CI,
and every entry fails CI from its expires date (UTC), so each one is re-reviewed rather than forgotten.
2026-10-03: 71 advisories in 20 packages. 2026-10-04: a lockfile-only update (npm update of the advisory
packages; no package.json change) fixed 62 of them without moving any native module. npm audit fix fixed
fewer and moved 12 native modules (expo 54.0.30 to 54.0.37, expo-updates, expo-notifications, expo-modules-core
and others), which would need a new App Store binary. The 9 left need an Expo SDK major (image-size, postcss),
an aws-amplify bump that changes bundled sign-in code (fast-xml-parser), or an upstream release that does not
exist yet (node-forge, braces); each reason says which. Delete an entry when npm stops reporting it.
Each entry's inBundle says whether its package is in the exported app. All 9 are false: their code runs only at
build time (Metro, @expo/cli, @expo/metro-config), or, for fast-xml-parser, sits under @aws-amplify/analytics, which
the app's aws-amplify imports never reach (it is not in the bundle either), so none of it reaches a device.
infra/scripts/check-bundle-packages.py enforces this in every run of the mobile CI job: it reads the source map of
every iOS and Android bundle file of that job's expo export (the main bundle and any split chunk), names each
bundled package directory as npm audit does (from package-lock.json, so an npm alias counts as its real package),
and fails if the package of any inBundle false entry is in either platform. A new entry must say true or false, or
both checks fail.
2026-10-04 re-review (owner decision, delegated to the supervisor): no Expo SDK upgrade before the 2.0.0 release,
so all 9 now expire on 2027-02-01 instead of 2026-11-03. The date stands for the next Expo SDK upgrade, which
moves Metro and @expo/metro-config (image-size, postcss) and may also drop micromatch (braces) or move @expo/cli's
node-forge: run npm audit --omit=dev in that change, delete every entry it clears and re-review the rest. The 3
fast-xml-parser entries need no SDK upgrade: they clear with the aws-amplify lockfile update (npm update
aws-amplify), shipped by its own OTA after a sign-in test on a device; delete them in that change.
check-npm-audit.py warns in every run from 14 days before an entry expires (from 2027-01-18). From 2027-02-01
(UTC) an entry still listed fails this check, main cannot merge and CD stops until it is fixed or re-reviewed.
evidence: 2026-10-04, mobile @ origin/main ebc2c10 plus the 2026-10-04 lockfile, npm 11.6.0: npm audit --omit=dev flagged
58 packages, most only because they depend on another one; underneath are 9 high or critical advisories in 5
packages (below). npx expo export --platform ios --platform android --source-maps bundled 146 package directories
on each platform (143 packages: buffer, react-is and scheduler have two copies each), and none of the 5 is among
them; the same on origin/main 63b5275 (two dev-only lockfile bumps later). The mobile CI job repeats that export
and check on every run (check-bundle-packages.py, on the .hbc.map sources); locally, from mobile/: the same export
The 2026-10-04 lockfile changed three bundled packages (nanoid 3.3.11 to 3.3.19, uuid 11.1.0 to 11.1.1, hasown
2.0.2 to 2.0.4, whose bundled index.js is unchanged); no package entered or left the bundle. An unminified export
(--no-minify --no-bytecode --source-maps --clear, each run with its own TMPDIR: Metro's transform cache in
$TMPDIR/metro-cache is shared between checkouts and its key does not include the @babel/* version), compared module
by module, differs in six modules on each platform; two runs of each tree are identical. Three carry the fixes:
nanoid's non-secure loop guard and uuid's buffer bounds check (v35.js, v6.js). Three come from the @babel/* 7.28 to
7.29 update and are semantically equivalent: a moved comment in @sentry/core utils/tracing.js, whitespace inside a
template-literal expression in @react-navigation/core useNavigationBuilder.js, and in
@revenuecat/purchases-js-hybrid-mappings (react-native-purchases uses it only in Expo Go and on web) one destructured
arrow parameter compiled to a _ref variable, which renumbers the later _refN names. The Sentry debug id changes too.
expo-modules-autolinking resolve and react-native-config output (iOS and Android) is identical before and after.

entries.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app (inBundle false): absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps, checked in every CI run by check-bundle-packages.py. Build-time only: expo > metro-file-map > micromatch glob matching in Metro, on repo-controlled patterns. No fixed release: the advisory covers <=3.0.3 and 3.0.3 is the newest braces; it leaves the tree only when Metro stops using micromatch (npm proposes react-native 0.87.1, a major).

entries.title: fast-xml-parser affected by numeric entity expansion bypassing all entity expansion limits (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-26278)
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app (inBundle false): absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps, checked in every CI run by check-bundle-packages.py. aws-amplify > @aws-amplify/analytics > @aws-sdk/client-firehose, client-kinesis and client-personalize-events > @aws-sdk/core 3.621.0, which pins fast-xml-parser 4.4.1 exactly; the app imports only Amplify (for Amplify.configure) from aws-amplify, and aws-amplify/auth. The top-level copy (4.5.7, @aws-amplify/storage) is already fixed. The fix is lockfile-only (npm update aws-amplify: 6.15.9 to 6.22.1), but it also changes bundled sign-in code (@aws-amplify/auth 6.17.1 to 6.21.1, @aws-amplify/core 6.15.0 to 6.19.2), so it is left for its own OTA after a sign-in test on a device.

entries.title: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app (inBundle false): absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps, checked in every CI run by check-bundle-packages.py. Build-time only: expo > metro reads the dimensions of the repo's own image assets. No lockfile fix: every metro 0.83.x (Expo SDK 54, through @expo/metro 54.2.0) requires image-size ^1.0.2, and 1.2.1, the newest 1.x, is affected (both advisories end at 2.0.2). It leaves with the Expo SDK major that moves Metro.

entries.title: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app (inBundle false): absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps, checked in every CI run by check-bundle-packages.py. Build-time only: @expo/cli dev-server certificates and @expo/code-signing-certificates; app.json sets no updates code signing. No fixed release: the advisory covers <=1.4.0 and 1.4.0 (2026-03-24) is the newest node-forge. The 2026-10-04 lockfile moved 1.3.3 to 1.4.0, which cleared the other four node-forge advisories.

entries.title: PostCSS: Arbitrary file read and information disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL in CSS comments
entries.reason: Not in the shipped app (inBundle false): absent from the iOS and Android Metro source maps, checked in every CI run by check-bundle-packages.py. Build-time only: @expo/metro-config's CSS transform; the app ships no CSS. No lockfile fix: every @expo/metro-config 54.0.x (pinned exactly by expo) requires postcss ~8.4.32, and 8.4.49, the newest 8.4.x, is affected; @expo/metro-config 57 moves to ^8.5.14. It leaves with an Expo SDK major.
